context_prefix_rationale: TSK_ENSD_* is consumed by SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC_v1 (29 tasks). Using EWRP_ (Engineered Wood RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_EWRP_* has zero existing usage. Pattern follows convention: EW = engineered wood, RP = repaint. FCRP_ already taken by SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted exterior engineered wood siding (LP SmartSide lap and panel profiles). Covers assessment (condition rating, adhesion test, chalk test, moisture probe, edge seal integrity check, caulk assessment per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol), low-pressure wash (500-1000 PSI OK for engineered wood — departure from FC's 400-600 PSI limit), condition-driven prep (scrape/feather failing areas, chalk remediation, degloss/scuff sound paint, mildew treatment), caulk assessment and replacement at siding-to-trim joints (butt joints assessed but NOT re-caulked per NC moisture trap prohibition), edge seal integrity verification (RP assessment — not application), state-driven primer (chalk-binding for SS_EXT_CHALKING, acrylic stain-block for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING, bonding primer on exposed ExpertFinish substrate), finish coat application (spray_backroll primary — 2-person crew, brush_roll fallback), interstage protocol, final inspection, landscape/hardscape protection, and RRP containment for pre-1978. Uses SF as primary UOM with siding profile modifier (lap/panel — NO shingle for engineered wood) and surface texture modifier (smooth/textured — 2 textures vs FC's 3). Access type drives height modifier per elevation. QT2-QT4 (QT5 excluded per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4). Sheens: flat, satin. 4 exterior RP substrate states. Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR drives prep intensity. Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978. spray_backroll is primary RP method (departure from NC spray-only for smooth profiles). Single mobilization.

relevant_findings.topic: Engineered wood RP uses spray_backroll as primary method — departure from NC spray-only
relevant_findings.finding: NC engineered wood siding uses spray as primary method for smooth profiles and spray_backroll mandatory only for T1-11. In RP context, the existing paint film has weathering, micro-cracking, and surface imperfections. Spray_backroll is the correct primary method for ALL RP engineered wood profiles: spray for coverage speed, backroll to work product into surface irregularities for maximum adhesion on the weathered existing film. This follows the established fiber cement RP pattern (SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP uses spray_backroll primary). brush_roll is fallback for <750 SF, occupied-adjacent, or high wind. spray-only is NOT valid for RP.

relevant_findings.topic: Low-pressure power wash IS allowed on engineered wood — unlike fiber cement
relevant_findings.finding: Engineered wood siding CAN be power washed at low pressure (500-1000 PSI) for RP prep. This is a KEY DEPARTURE from fiber cement RP which prohibits power washing entirely and uses only garden hose rinse at 400-600 PSI max. Engineered wood's resin-bonded wood strand surface tolerates gentle power washing without the texture damage risk that fiber cement faces. However, HIGH PRESSURE (>1000 PSI) remains prohibited — forces water into OSB core at joints and cut edges, causing irreversible swelling/springback. NC spec prohibits ALL power washing because factory primer is intact and only needs gentle cleaning. RP has existing weathered paint film that benefits from power wash for surface preparation.

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to engineered wood siding
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (adhered, minimal chalk — degloss/scuff only), SS_EXT_CHALKING (surface chalk present — chalk-binding primer mandatory), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking/alligatoring — scrape/feather + spot or full prime), SS_EXT_PEELING (active coating lifting — heavy scrape + full prime). SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded — weathered bare engineered wood with no coating is NC territory. NC substrate states (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY, SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD, SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED, SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD) are NOT valid for RP. Per-elevation substrate state if conditions differ.

relevant_findings.topic: Edge seal integrity check is an RP assessment task — not application
relevant_findings.finding: NC spec includes TSK_ENSD_SEAL_CUT_EDGES as a critical application task (sealing ALL field-cut edges to prevent OSB core springback FM-001). In RP, edges were sealed during original installation. The RP task is an ASSESSMENT of edge seal integrity: inspect cut edges at butt joints, miters, and field cuts for signs of failed edge seal (swelling, springback, soft spots). If edge seal has failed, the resulting damage is visible and addressed through scraping, repair, and spot priming. Edge seal re-application on intact joints is NOT an RP task. Edge seal assessment is an RP_NEW task replacing the NC edge seal application task.

relevant_findings.topic: NO alkali-resistant primer needed for engineered wood — neutral pH substrate
relevant_findings.finding: KEY DEPARTURE from fiber cement RP: when paint fails on engineered wood and scraping exposes bare substrate, the exposed OSB-core engineered wood is NEUTRAL pH (wood-based, not cementitious). Standard acrylic stain-block primer is correct for exposed bare engineered wood areas. Alkali-resistant primer is NOT needed and NOT valid for this spec. This simplifies the primer path compared to FC RP which requires alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC at pH 13.0.

relevant_findings.topic: Bonding primer path exists for exposed ExpertFinish factory-finished substrate
relevant_findings.finding: Previously painted LP SmartSide ExpertFinish (factory-finished, then field-painted during NC) presents a unique RP substrate: when RP paint fails and scraping exposes the original oven-baked factory finish underneath the field paint, the exposed factory finish requires bonding primer — same as NC SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED. This is a secondary/rare primer path. Most RP engineered wood siding will be standard factory-primed-then-painted, not ExpertFinish.
relevant_findings.source: SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json (ExpertFinish bonding primer); SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1/research.json RF-007 (factory-finish in RP)

relevant_findings.topic: Siding profiles: lap and panel only — NO shingle, NO T1-11 in RP
relevant_findings.finding: Engineered wood siding profiles for RP: lap and panel only. NO shingle (engineered wood doesn't come in shingle — that's fiber cement only). NO T1-11 in the RP profile set because T1-11 is primarily a new-construction panel that was commonly used on older homes NOT typically repainted to RP standard (replaced instead). If T1-11 RP is encountered, it would be very rare and warrants separate T&M consideration. NC spec includes T1-11 with 1.80x profile modifier. RP drops T1-11 for simplicity. Profile modifiers for RP: lap=1.00x, panel=0.90x (panel is slightly faster in RP — spray_backroll on large flat areas is efficient, same as FC RP pattern).

relevant_findings.topic: Surface textures: smooth and textured only — 2 textures vs NC's 3
relevant_findings.finding: NC engineered wood siding has 3 surface textures: smooth (1.00x), cedarmill (1.20x), roughsawn (1.30x). For RP, the texture distinction matters less on an already-painted surface — the existing paint film has obscured original texture differences over previous paint cycles. RP uses 2 textures: smooth (1.00x) and textured (1.15x). 'Textured' combines cedarmill and roughsawn into a single modifier because the existing paint film moderates the difference between them. This follows the FC RP pattern which uses 3 textures but with compressed modifiers.
relevant_findings.source: SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json (3 textures); SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (texture modifiers in RP)

relevant_findings.topic: Moisture sensitivity is HIGHER for engineered wood than fiber cement in RP
relevant_findings.finding: Engineered wood is MORE moisture-sensitive than fiber cement. The OSB core absorbs water through failed paint, failed edge seals, and joints. MC check before coating is mandatory at ALL quality tiers (same as NC). Moisture content must be <15% before any coating. NC has a dedicated TSK_ENSD_MOISTURE_CHECK task — this transfers as MODIFIED to RP (different context: checking existing paint film permeability + edge seal integrity rather than post-wash dry time).

relevant_findings.topic: Caulk scope in RP: siding-to-trim joints assessed and replaced, butt joints assessed only
relevant_findings.finding: NC spec explicitly prohibits caulking field butt joints (creates moisture trap against OSB core per RF-012 in NC research). RP caulk assessment follows 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol on ALL joints including butt joints — because previous installers or painters may have caulked butt joints, and failed caulk is an active water intrusion point. RP ASSESSES butt joint caulk condition but follows the NC prohibition: failed butt joint caulk is REMOVED but NOT re-caulked (remove moisture trap). Siding-to-trim joints (corner boards, window/door casings, frieze) are fully assessed and replaced as needed.
relevant_findings.source: SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json (NO caulk on butt joints); Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine; SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1/research.json RF-006

relevant_findings.topic: RRP lead-safe requirements — more common for engineered wood than fiber cement
relevant_findings.finding: LP SmartSide engineered wood siding entered the market in the late 1990s, so the material itself is post-1978. However, engineered wood siding is sometimes installed as replacement on pre-1978 structures, and the pre-1978 flag is project-level. RRP is more likely to be triggered for engineered wood RP than fiber cement RP because engineered wood siding was also produced by earlier manufacturers (Louisiana-Pacific InnerSeal, pre-SmartSide era, 1990s). Some of these early products may be on homes with pre-1978 structures that had lead paint on the original siding. RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance.
relevant_findings.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RRP pattern); SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json RC-001 (RRP = 2.0x)

relevant_findings.topic: Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR maps to substrate states and drives prep intensity
relevant_findings.finding: GOOD = SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep). FAIR = SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.5x prep). POOR = SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (2.0x prep). Modifiers apply to prep tasks ONLY — never coating tasks. Same pattern as FC RP.

relevant_findings.topic: LP SmartSide manufacturer warranty requires specific paint systems in RP
relevant_findings.finding: LP SmartSide warranty requires 100% acrylic exterior latex for finish coats. LP-approved products include Sherwin-Williams Duration, Benjamin Moore Regal Select. The warranty originally required minimum 2 topcoats on NC; for RP the warranty requires proper surface preparation and compatible coating systems. QT2 economy single-coat RP is outside LP warranty coverage. Note this in compatibility rules.
relevant_findings.source: LP SmartSide Technical Documentation; SF_SIDING_ENGINEERED_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json (LP warranty notes)

relevant_findings.topic: Customer walkthrough is RP-specific — occupied home context
relevant_findings.finding: RP siding work occurs on occupied homes. Customer walkthrough after completion is a standard RP task: walk each elevation with homeowner, verify color/sheen satisfaction, document completion. FIXED task per project (~15-20 min).

relevant_findings.topic: Mildew treatment is an RP-specific prep task
relevant_findings.finding: Engineered wood siding in humid climates develops surface mildew and algae, especially on north-facing and shaded elevations. Mildew must be killed before painting — painting over mildew causes topcoat failure. Treatment: biocide solution, 10-15 min dwell, power rinse. RP_NEW task.

condition_drivers.effect: Primary prep intensity driver. GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual inspection + adhesion test + chalk test + moisture probe + edge seal check. Per-elevation rating.

condition_drivers.effect: Moderate/heavy chalk = chalk-binding primer mandatory. Light chalk may resolve after power wash.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: White cloth rub test after power wash. Moderate residue = chalk-binding primer required.

condition_drivers.effect: Failed caulk = water intrusion. Moderate scope for engineered wood — siding-to-trim joints only (butt joints assessed but not re-caulked per NC prohibition).
condition_drivers.assessment_method: 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol per elevation.

condition_drivers.effect: EW-specific. Failed edge seal = OSB core exposure → moisture → springback. Assessment determines if repair needed.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual + probe at all visible cut edges, butt joints, field cuts.

condition_drivers.effect: Biocide treatment task activation. Common on north-facing/shaded elevations.

key_departures_from_nc: Application method: spray_backroll replaces spray as primary (all profiles). spray-only NOT valid for RP.
Wash method: low-pressure power wash (500-1000 PSI) allowed for RP — NC prohibits all power washing.
Edge seal: NC seals all cut edges (application). RP checks edge seal integrity (assessment).
Substrate states: 4 RP states (SOUND_PAINT/CHALKING/FAILING_PAINT/PEELING) replace 4 NC states.
Profiles: lap/panel only — T1-11 dropped for RP. Panel modifier changes from 1.10x to 0.90x.
Textures: smooth/textured (2) replace smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn (3). Paint film obscures original texture.
Assessment module: 6 RP_NEW tasks for condition evaluation. NC has no assessment.
Condition scale: GOOD/FAIR/POOR (1.0x/1.5x/2.0x) drives prep intensity. NC has no condition modifier.
Caulk scope: 2-step (remove failed + apply new) vs NC 1-step (apply only at trim joints).
RRP module: lead-safe containment for pre-1978. NC has no RRP.
Customer walkthrough: RP-specific occupied home task. NC does not include.
Primer paths: chalk-binding + acrylic stain-block + bonding. NC has acrylic + bonding only.
NO alkali-resistant primer — engineered wood is neutral pH (key departure from FC RP).
key_departures_from_fc_rp: Power wash OK at 500-1000 PSI (FC RP prohibits all power washing — 400-600 PSI rinse only).
NO alkali-resistant primer needed (engineered wood neutral pH vs FC pH 13.0).
NO efflorescence treatment (EW is not cementitious — no mineral salt deposits).
Edge seal integrity check replaces edge seal application (EW-specific RP assessment).
Profiles: lap/panel only (no shingle — EW doesn't come in shingle).
Moisture check MORE critical — EW OSB core is more moisture-sensitive than FC.
Butt joint caulk REMOVED but NOT replaced (FC butt joints assessed and may be re-caulked in RP).
LP SmartSide warranty compliance vs James Hardie warranty compliance.
